# Workspace Task creation and current reads

**Artifact ID:** WORKSPACE-TASKS-01\
**Version/date:** 0.3 Draft · 4 November 2026\
**Status:** Local bounded implementation/runbook; no deployment or independent acceptance.\
**Historical SP-03 inputs:** [FEAT-SP03-01](../../docs/implementation/features/sp-03-create-task/plan.md) v0.5; canonical SP-03 v0.8; Workspace v0.2.12; logical model v0.12; Proposed ADR-0027 v0.2.

Current operations: POST /projects/{project_id}/tasks, GET the same collection (location=all or backlog; optional cursor), GET /tasks/{task_id}. Session/project prerequisites remain in [SESSION-HTTP.md](SESSION-HTTP.md) and [PROJECTS.md](PROJECTS.md); use the existing [same-origin HTTPS setup](../../apps/web/LOCAL-HTTPS.md). Browser calls only the Workspace /api facade. No Task edit/reorder/assignment/state/blocker/Sprint/Knowledge/AI mutation is implemented here.

## Storage and explicit setup

Task routes require additive Workspace 009. Startup never migrates, initializes clock/accounts or grants authority. Follow the [storage runbook](../../infra/postgres/README.md); these checks upgraded only uniquely named disposable databases, not development storage. Applied 001–008 remain unchanged. Historical session/storage fixtures keep 006 and SP-02 keeps 007/008; Task fixtures explicitly request 009.

009 refuses existing Task rows, createTask identities or backlog-author grants before DDL. It never invents legacy time, adopts an unprovenanced grant or deletes retained data. Reconcile valuable legacy data through a separately reviewed forward recovery; this migration does not supply guessed backfill. Empty-compatible down restores prior constraints, but retained Task/history/outcome/author/audit data blocks it. The root rollback command reverses more than this migration; do not use it as an incidental Task reset.

Creation returns immutable server `created_at`, exact decimal Backlog position, todo/null-assignee/unblocked/revision 1 and a server UUID. Project guard serializes max(current Backlog position)+1; existing 003 advances generation once. The Task, UC-03 business audit `backlog-item-create` (actor/entity/same creation time/correlation) and permanent original result commit together. Idempotency operation is `createTask`; it is deliberately distinct from the audit event label. Draft 009 down retains both that canonical label and the earlier draft audit alias.

## Private author provisioning

An enabled authenticated current member needs an explicit project-scoped `backlog-author` grant. PO/Admin/creator role text and membership-manage do not grant it. No automatic creator grant, permission editor or public provisioning endpoint exists. Runtime may invalidate an author on member removal; the ordinary runtime database role cannot issue or revive one.

Use the existing private operator environment described in PROJECTS.md: SACW_OPERATOR_DATABASE_URL and SACW_OPERATOR_REF, never a browser role or credentials in argv/logs. Node 24+ accepts bounded JSON on stdin:

```powershell
'{"user_id":"<enabled-current-member-uuid>","project_id":"<project-uuid>"}' | node services/workspace/src/projects/cli.ts state
'{"user_id":"<enabled-current-member-uuid>","project_id":"<project-uuid>","action":"backlog-author","allowed":true,"expected_revision":"0","reason":"Explicit project author provisioning"}' | node services/workspace/src/projects/cli.ts project
```

Select the latest revision for backlog-author from state; absence means 0. Do not reuse a manager/global revision. Revoke with allowed=false and the current revision. Changes co-commit private audit; no-op grants do not create another grant/audit. Last-author revoke is allowed; the existing last membership-manager safeguard is separate. Removal invalidates grants and rejoin restores none. An uncertain operator acknowledgement requires inspecting the same target/revision/private audit before retry, not provisioning a role bypass.

## Read and recovery boundary

Current membership is checked for detail/list, current author authority again for create/replay. Unknown and inaccessible reads share generic 404; an existing readable project without create authority returns 403. Session/clock/DB/key failures withhold output. Detail resolves an internal scope hint, then locks Project and re-reads Task; no Task-first lock.

All lists use Task UUID order. Backlog uses PostgreSQL numeric position then UUID and includes Done Backlog tasks. `work_location`, highest committed blocker sequence and exact `backlog_revision` come from current owned data. Page size is internally 50; no public limit query exists. Reuse SACW_PROJECT_CURSOR_KEY and its 300-second default TTL. Actor/project/filter/order/membership/full ordered projection and Backlog generation bind the cursor. Malformed/foreign tokens return 400, verified expired/stale/missing bookmarks 409 without items; the UI discards accumulation and loads the current first page. Full-projection hashing has no scalability/load acceptance claim. Cooperating writers must retain the Project/clock protocol; this does not prove D-07 socket exclusion.

Consumed key/hash plus original minimal Task 201 snapshot (including original title/description/time) are retained indefinitely without automatic expiry/recycling. Current access is rechecked before every replay. A later Task change never rewrites that snapshot. UI validates confirmed replay, then separately fetches current detail; a historical receipt is not current work state. Strict old Task validators may reject the required new created_at field: consumers must use the coordinated Workspace 0.2.12 schema.

Before sending, browser tab storage retains only the actor-bound original request/key/body, not credentials/tokens or fetched protected lists. Timeout, dropped response or denied reconciliation does not prove rollback; check the original creation and never create a new automatic key. Explicit sign-out clears pending input. Same-actor re-login can reconcile after expiry; current denial keeps the earlier result unknown. Storage failure prevents sending a mutation while reads remain available.

## Verification

Use the existing installation with Node 24+ active. These commands create/clean only their uniquely identified synthetic containers/volumes:

```powershell
npm run typecheck
npm run build
node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/workspace/task-storage.test.mjs tests/workspace/task-authority.test.mjs tests/workspace/task-http.test.mjs tests/workspace/task-reads.test.mjs tests/workspace/task-concurrency.test.mjs tests/workspace/task-ui-controller.test.mjs tests/workspace/task-ui.test.mjs
```

The separate browser command is `node --test tests/workspace/task-browser.test.mjs`. Supply the already installed Playwright entry URL through SACW_PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE if it is not locally resolvable, installed Edge and the existing owner-trusted localhost certificate. NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS may reference that specific public certificate for the Node forwarding probe. No TLS bypass, personal profile, package/browser install or incidental trust-store change is part of the test. Missing prerequisites fail, never pass as a skip. Each successful browser attempt writes a unique evidence run directory and preserves earlier captures.

Run the four session suites and test:projects with their retained ceilings for regression. Schema/context/docs checks are separate from actual handler/DB/DOM/browser assertions. [Actual execution report](../../docs/sdlc/reports/SP-03-2026-11-02-execution.md) records final commands/source hashes, prior failures, measured boundaries and unrun broader gates. No fresh-install, all-browser/accessibility, independent review, full scenario/release/deployment or newly published GitHub runtime claim is made.

## SP-04 P03B additive010 storage support — 4 November 2026

[FEAT-SP04-01](../../docs/implementation/features/sp-04-update-task/plan.md) and [SP04-P03B](../../docs/implementation/features/sp-04-update-task/tasks/P03B-mutation-storage.md) own current execution/evidence under [Proposed ADR-0028](../../docs/adr/0028-task-mutation-authority-and-outcomes.md). New010 adds typed immutable permanent original editTask/setTaskState/setAssignee200 Task and recordBlocker201 Blocker, preserving009 creation/project/member/protected outcomes. Stored Task originals include title/description; replay callers must recheck current session, Task/project read scope and exact action. The internal adapter is not a permission check and never substitutes live revision/state/assignee for an original result.

New project-scoped task-edit/task-state/task-assign/task-blocker grants have private DB issue/revival and current uniqueness/scope protection. Runtime may only invalidate an existing selected grant with its next revision and unchanged identity, as actual member removal does; rejoin restores none. At the historical P03B checkpoint the operator/CLI did not yet provision these actions; current P03C support is described below. No mutation/history HTTP handler or UI is introduced by P03B.

010 refuses pre-existing selected operation keys/grants/audits or blocker history requiring explicit reconciliation; old SP-03 Task/create-result/author data stays compatible. Down refuses retained new operation results, even invalidated selected grants, authority/business audit or blocker history. Empty-compatible reverse restores the exact009 original-outcome constraint/function, without editing001–009. No automatic legacy backfill, evidence purge or development upgrade is supplied. Startup never migrates.

Run only the explicit disposable suite with existing Node24+ and Docker:

```powershell
node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/workspace/task-mutation-storage.test.mjs
node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/workspace/task-storage.test.mjs
```

The new fixture explicitly requests010 (or009 for upgrade/refusal tests). Existing Task/session/project fixture ceilings remain009/006/008. Fixtures generate synthetic identities/secrets and random named container/volume resources, cleaning only their own verified resources; never use global Docker cleanup or the valuable-data rollback command as a test reset. Actual passes/failures/source identities and unrun gates are recorded by the owning plan/report, not inferred from these commands.

## SP-04 P03C private action tooling and Task discovery — 4 November 2026

The existing private project command now also accepts task-edit, task-state, task-assign and task-blocker, with current enabled account/membership, expected revision, explicit reason and private operator provenance. No action is inherited from creator, backlog-author, role text or another Task action. Use the existing private operator configuration, never browser input or database credentials in command arguments. Example:

```powershell
'{"user_id":"<enabled-current-member-uuid>","project_id":"<project-uuid>","action":"task-edit","allowed":true,"expected_revision":"0","reason":"Explicit Backlog edit authority"}' | node services/workspace/src/projects/cli.ts project
'{"user_id":"<enabled-current-member-uuid>","project_id":"<project-uuid>"}' | node services/workspace/src/projects/cli.ts state
```

Revoke with allowed=false and the current highest action revision. Grant/revoke and its private audit commit atomically; unchanged requests are no-ops and stale revisions deny. A selected grant issuance uses one UUID for grant_id and its private issue audit event_id, binding project/subject/action/original revision without new schema. Existing selected rows without matching immutable issue evidence are retained and rejected for explicit reconciliation, including apparent no-ops. Ordinary runtime never reads this private audit. Existing three capability actions retain their previous audit encoding. Removal invalidates current grants, rejoin restores none, and an explicit later regrant uses a fresh ID/revision/audit.

GET /access/allowed-actions?resource_kind=task&project_id=<project-uuid>&resource_id=<task-uuid> now resolves current membership and the exact same-project Task, returning existing AllowedActions fields, only public operation IDs and Cache-Control:no-store. Missing/foreign/nonmember targets share generic404; malformed or contradictory selectors use bounded400; unavailable authority uses503 without cached allow. A final session guard runs after lock waits. The response contains no grant IDs/reasons, title, revision or authority token and cannot authorise a later write.

Production currently advertises getTask for readable Task targets, plus getAllowedActions itself. New mutation/history handlers are still absent and are not advertised, even when their private grants exist. The shared Workspace policy mapping prepares their capability/context filtering; future producers must explicitly register actual handlers and independently check current read/action authority for every write/replay. Edit discovery is Backlog-only; history read needs operational read, not audit-read. Synthetic future-operation registries in tests are projection tests, not implemented HTTP handlers.

Run the new010 disposable authority/discovery suite directly:

```powershell
node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/workspace/task-mutation-authority.test.mjs
```

[SP04-P03C](../../docs/implementation/features/sp-04-update-task/tasks/P03C-task-authority-discovery.md) and its parent own actual evidence, regressions and limits. CLI failures do not prove rollback after a lost acknowledgement; inspect the same target/revision/private audit before retrying. No startup migration, valuable-data upgrade or public provisioning endpoint is added.

For each new plan: replace the empty row with the actual ID/link, register the artifact centrally and in the [source register](../register.md), and add the roadmap backlink. Keep one canonical task table per feature. Parent rows reference it; they do not copy every task's mutable status.

## Saved plan template

Create `<work-id>/README.md`, `<work-id>/plan.md` and `<work-id>/tasks/<task-id>-<slug>.md`. Copy the structure below into plan.md and replace placeholders before calling a task ready. State kind as feature, fix, hotfix or test. Link each task row to its individual file; each task file records source versions, parent/child IDs, dependencies, allowed paths, steps, acceptance assertions, actual-versus-planned commands and result/handoff requirements. Keep execution state only in the parent plan table. Short plans retain the same structure; missing commands are Planned, never reported as executed.

```markdown
# <Feature name>

**Artifact ID:** <unique plan ID>
**Version/date:** 0.1 Draft · <date>
**Status:** Planning / Ready for authorised tasks / In progress / Verification gaps
**Inputs:** <source versions and links, including spec/contracts/ADRs>
**Trace:** <FR/AC/BR/SC and relevant UC/TC>
**Owner role:** Sequential implementer
**Planning mode:** Plan mode used / unavailable (state the actual limitation)
**Work kind:** feature / fix / hotfix / test

## Goal, scope and parent registration

Observable outcome:
Fix/hotfix: observed failure, reproduction/incident evidence, regression assertion:
Hotfix: recovery/rollback and any deferred verification/follow-up task IDs:
Testing: environment/fixtures, expected assertions, evidence destination, triage tasks:
Non-goals:
Parent PLAN-01 section (link):
Parent roadmap milestone (link):
Canonical spec / implementation pack and child IDs (links):
Feature register / central register / source register links:
Existing authorisation and material open decisions:

## Implementation boundaries

Allowed paths copied from canonical spec:
Owning service and integration consumers:
Existing implementation/conventions to reuse:
Dependencies, migration/contract changes and coordinated scope updates:
Permission, version, citation, audit and failure/unknown-outcome constraints:

## Tasks

| Task ID | Reviewable outcome | Depends on / decision gates | Allowed paths | Acceptance assertions / verification | Status / result link |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <feature-id>-T01 | <one concrete outcome> | <ready prerequisites> | <bounded paths> | <observable positive/negative checks> | Not started |

## Integration and feature acceptance

Must AC → task/assertion mapping:
End-to-end, negative/concurrency/failure and UI coverage as applicable:
Existing verification commands vs Planned commands:
Evidence boundary (schema/SQL/lab handlers vs application handlers):
Unrun checks and unresolved decisions:

## Handoff and change log

Next ready task and prerequisites:
Actual results/handoff links using the existing handoff template:
Source/plan revisions and downstream registration changes:
Owner acceptance or independent review only if actually obtained:
```

Use existing [execution states and evidence rules](../execution.md) and [handoff template](../handoff-template.md). A plan/task may be ready for authorised work while a separate dependency remains open; list the boundary explicitly. Do not mark the whole feature verified from preparation or a structural check.

**Checklist:** Self-checked for the planning/register/template contract; runtime verification N/A because this file adds no handler. **Handoff:** start feature/fix/hotfix/test work through a saved or updated registered plan.

- A timeout is unknown outcome, not rollback. Reconcile the original scoped identity/payload. A protected AI transport follows its one-use/unknown-transport rules, not generic mutation replay.
- Do not simplify by removing guards, content permissions, durable evidence, history or tests. Revisit unnecessary mechanism complexity through the decision process.
- Later milestone preparation may use local synthetic doubles. It does not authorise live AI relay before the work/document gates.
- No additional Must deferral, automatic graph, meeting AI, reports expansion or runtime multi-agent feature is introduced.

# Central diagram index

**Artifact ID:** UML-07
**Version/date:** 0.21.2 Draft · 3 November 2026
**Status:** Draft; Ready for downstream inventory use; C4 primary views with a 4+1 coverage crosswalk are recommended; see the 17 October report for corrections and remaining design/implementation gates.
**Source versions:** BRD English v1.0; PRD-01 v0.10.1; UC-02 v0.8.2; SAD-03 v0.16.2; UX Docs v0.9 / sitemap v0.10 / personas v0.5 / matrix v0.11 / Board v0.10 / AI v0.9; ADR-0004 v0.2; ADR-0007–ADR-0017; Proposed ADR-0018–ADR-0023; PLAN-01 v0.4.

## Historical Diagram-first design foundation — 17 October 2026

Start with the [design foundation and reading order](design-foundation-2026-10-17.md): eleven additional pairs cover C4 Context/Container, protected handoff and document creation sequences, lifecycle states, per-store physical ERDs, the logical evidence gap, local deployment and package ownership. The same set provides 4+1 coverage. Proposed application behavior is distinguished from implemented storage. Review and acceptance limits are recorded in that report.

## Historical owner decisions — 16 October 2026

[OWNER-Q-01](../../planning/owner-decisions-2026-10-16.md) confirms To Do on unfinished Backlog returns and manifest persistence before guard. DGM-FLOW-02 v0.7 labels Completed-Sprint reopening as Backlog / To Do; DGM-FLOW-01 v0.9 and DGM-FLOW-05 v0.4 show immutable manifests outside guard, then exact guarded validation through handoff. A stale attempt releases the guard before fresh preparation. All paired labels match; real transaction/transport enforcement remains unimplemented.

## Maintaining generated metadata

Edit `manifest.json` for registered IDs, versions, paths, origin/source IDs, ADR sets and operation references. Edit diagram meaning in its Mermaid/native pair, then run `npm run docs:sync-metadata` and `npm run docs:lint`. Sync preserves native geometry and diagram bodies while generating headers, titles, child READMEs and the marked inventory/version-table regions here and in the Register. Child indexes and generated regions have no separate handwritten version authority. Lint checks those outputs without writing and rejects any unregistered Mermaid or native source, including use cases.

Use-case associations, hollow-triangle generalization and dashed `«include»` relations have a dedicated adapter; they are not forced into directed-flowchart semantics. ADR-set lint expands shorthand/ranges and checks every literal body ADR in registered diagram Sources, in both formats. Unselected retrieval terms require “unselected” or “not adopted” in the same Markdown line or native label; migrations may not introduce them. The current [DGM-REVIEW-03](review-2026-10-17.md) records source corrections, C4/4+1 guidance and fresh export evidence. DGM-REVIEW-02 and DGM-REVIEW-01 remain historical snapshots.

## Historical search-path correction — 16 October 2026

DGM-ARCH-01 v0.9 separates PostgreSQL English full-text search (GIN) — independent keyword path — from pgvector exact AI discovery. DGM-FLOW-01 v0.9 labels the AI and fallback paths separately and makes search an explicit user choice after AI failure. Both editable formats were updated. Trigram/fusion remains unselected pending pilot evidence and a separate ADR. Both Draw.io diagrams exported successfully and their overviews were inspected: the architecture branches are readable; the AI flow remains wide with long return routes and needs print-scale review. No runtime behaviour follows from the diagram checks.

Latest diagnostic exports (untracked) use `.tmp/review-diagrams/metadata-DGM-*.png`: all nine registered diagrams exported and were inspected at overview scale. See DGM-REVIEW-02 for current results and open RV-09 routing/readability issues. Earlier OWNER-Q-01 exports use `qdecisions-*.png`; Board routing received targeted repairs in that earlier review.

## Historical policy correction — 14 October 2026

Follow-up: DGM-FLOW-01/03/04 v0.6 synchronize ADR-0013/15/16/17 in both formats: partial answers, verified unavailable citation identity, whole invalid-draft withholding, independent optional task search, and membership removal effects. Docs/read geometry is preserved pending rendered review. AI was exported and inspected; crossing edges prompted an ELK relayout. Its second render still has a wide layout and long return routes; practical readability remains open. Source comparisons and contract checks passed; this does not establish runtime behavior.

Docs flow now shows immediate Current revision and Workspace-first creation with an explicit author read grant. Source reads no longer have a Draft/content-write read bypass. Board labels include direct transitions and reopening from Completed Sprints without rewriting completion history. The illustrative journey saves a new Current instead of publishing. UC-07 and Content Author labels match UC-02 v0.5. AI/sitemap/architecture topology is retained with current source metadata. Both editable formats are updated; no rendered or independent acceptance is implied.

## Historical storage source reconciliation — 13 October 2026

DGM-ARCH-01 v0.4 refreshes its source/version metadata against SAD-03 v0.6 and ADR-0004 v0.2. Graph nodes, edges and layout are unchanged: owned database storage is implemented, while service HTTP/provider edges remain design. This source reconciliation is not rendered-layout acceptance or application evidence.

## Historical UX and diagram correction — 12 October 2026

Permission matrix/personas v0.3 use separate capabilities and project-shared/restricted classifications; journey v0.2 marks all actors/scores as synthetic. DGM-FLOW-04 v0.4 covers source/work reads; DGM-FLOW-05 v0.1 preserves four AI checkpoints, failure and bounded-retry exits. Citation opening returns to DGM-FLOW-04 and repeats all checks. Existing Proposed ADR-0001/ADR-0006 supply the rationale; no API or authority decision changes. Stage 5 wire mappings and owner policy decisions remain open.

The docs:lint command checks real Mermaid grammar, native XML, node labels and directed labelled edge multiplicity, journey sections/actors/scores/order, origin versions and current version tables. Unsupported diagram types fail explicitly. It does not establish claim support, policy enforcement, visual quality or independent approval. See REG-00 for execution evidence. # Bounded Task mutation authority, original outcomes and history

**Artifact ID:** ADR-0028\
**Version/date:** 0.1 Proposed · 3 November 2026\
**Status:** Proposed mechanics; three owner-selected policy directions have explicit provenance. No formal ADR, storage, handler, deployment or independent acceptance.\
**Inputs:** [SP04-OWNER-01](../implementation/features/sp-04-update-task/owner-decisions.md) v0.1 and its submitted-answer record; [SP04-DECISION-BATCH](../implementation/features/sp-04-update-task/decision-batch.md) v0.4; [P03A disposition](../implementation/features/sp-04-update-task/reviews/p03a-codex-disposition.md) v0.1; [owning plan](../implementation/features/sp-04-update-task/plan.md); Workspace OpenAPI v0.2.13; logical model v0.13; ADR-0008 v0.3 / ADR-0017 v0.2 owner-confirmed directions; Proposed ADR-0018 v0.2 / ADR-0019 v0.4 / ADR-0026 v0.4 / ADR-0027 v0.2.\
**Trace:** FR-09/40/43/44 and supporting FR-03/31/59/68; BR-01/02/03/06/10/11/14; UC-03 Alt-1/EX-03 and UC-04 main/Alt-1/Alt-2/EX-01–04; TC-07/08/13/14/16/18/19/22; SP-04.1–04.4 / PLAN-01 Month 1 / M-02–M-03.

## Context and owner directions

The current Workspace implements create/read Task, session and project/membership handlers. These four Task mutations and blocker history handlers remain absent. Existing private tooling provisions backlog-author for creation; it must not silently become edit authority. Existing 009 receipts permit original createTask201, not Task200/Blocker201 for new operations. The separate older SP-04 worktree is historical, not an adopted implementation.

The owner explicitly selected on 3 November 2026:

1. Provision edit authority separately; Task creator/create-only backlog-author receives no automatic edit right.
2. Reject new assignment to a disabled account even if its project membership remains active.
3. Retain original mutation outcomes indefinitely as in SP-03, including Task title/description, with current authority rechecked before disclosure.

These directions do not accept every proposed mechanism below. They do not change Core scope, FR priorities, document access, service ownership or read-only runtime AI.

## Proposed mechanics

### Authority and private provisioning

Use four explicit project-scoped action names: task-edit, task-state, task-assign and task-blocker. Resolve the exact current Task/project and require current session, membership, read scope and the requested action for new writes **and** committed replay. Role labels, creator, assignee, backlog-author and membership-manage imply none of these actions. Edit applies only to current Backlog work for new edits. Discovery reports public operation IDs only for registered handlers, current authority and applicable current context; it is advisory, never a reusable allow decision.

Extend private operator/CLI provisioning under workspace_owner with enabled current membership, expected grant revision, operator/reason provenance and atomic append-only audit. Enforce issue/revival restrictions in the DB as well as the CLI; runtime cannot issue/revive a selected grant. Enforce one current project/subject/action grant and reject unsupported legacy rows without deletion or guessed provenance. Membership removal invalidates selected grants atomically with existing assignee cleanup; rejoin restores neither. No public grant endpoint or implicit manager bypass is added.

### Transaction and original-outcome branches

Reuse the actual single-client owned transaction and existing clock/account/session validation in [Project store](../../services/workspace/src/projects/store.ts), [session store](../../services/workspace/src/session/store.ts) and existing cooperating removal/private writers. No Knowledge write, provider call or network wait belongs in the transaction.

After actor clock/account/session locks, read internal target/outcome hints without disclosing them. A committed identity takes the replay branch: verify current Task/project read/action authority and exact actor/operation/key/canonical-input/target/receipt binding, then final same-client session/time check before returning its immutable original result. Do not apply current write revision, old assignee eligibility or current placement as replay prerequisites, and do not mutate again. Changed payload conflicts. Current revocation denies historical disclosure; UI fetches current state separately.

A genuinely new non-null assignment locks the target account **before Project**, matching removeMember, then checks current actor membership/action, target membership and Task. Unknown target is an internal eligibility result; disclose only bounded validation after caller scope/action authorisation. Other new commands lock Project before Task; multi-Task writers use stable Task-ID order. Recheck outcomes at the stable boundary before write preconditions if needed. The current clock serializes cooperating writers; it does not prove capacity or universal deadlock freedom.

After relevant waits use the existing guard's false/typed-null path. A clock-fault latch/authentication audit actually produced by the guard must commit before denial is raised outside the wrapper; throwing inside would erase it. Ordinary expiry does not imply a fault audit. Recheck current expected revision and safe integer bounds for new writes. Actual business change, minimum business audit and durable original result commit together; persistence failure rolls back all business effects. Lost COMMIT/HTTP acknowledgement is unknown and reconciles with the same original identity/body, never a fresh automatic key. This is not D-07 source/socket-handoff proof.

### Typed immutable results and retention

Retain original editTask/setTaskState/setAssignee **200 Task** with result_ref=task_id and recordBlocker **201 Blocker** with result_ref=event_id indefinitely alongside consumed actor/operation/key/hash. No automatic expiry, key recycling or current-row substitution. Preserve existing createProject201/Project, addMember201/Member, removeMember204/null and createTask201/Task branches exactly; protected-handoff/other operation semantics remain unchanged.

Future additive storage must use total typed validators and explicit true enforcement. Reject missing/extra/wrong/null-ambiguous values, unsafe casts, invalid UUID/date/enum and non-safe positive integer revision/sequence. Task has its exact current wire fields including immutable millisecond UTC created_at, no updated_at. WorkLocation is exactly Backlog(kind,position) or Sprint/Completed(kind,sprint_id); Sprint locations have no position, and Completed receipts require the appropriate historical done state. Backlog position is an exact finite decimal string. Blocker has its exact current fields and actual wire timestamp serialization, not an invented precision rule. Bind identities without requiring an old receipt to equal mutable live state. Preserve correct OLD/NEW operation immutability and DELETE/UPDATE trigger returns, fixed search paths and least privileges.

New empty/same-value edit, same-state or same-assignee requests are business no-ops after current new-write preconditions, including target eligibility. Retain the original Task200 without Task revision bump or fake business-change audit; mandatory authentication fault evidence remains separate. Omitted edit field means unchanged, explicit null is invalid for nonnullable fields; omitted blocker outcome normalizes to null. Canonical hashing binds operation, route Task, original expected revision and exact semantic input, not arbitrary object property order. Every distinct valid blocker operation appends and increments Task revision, even if derived blocked stays the same; a committed retry appends nothing.

### Placement, history and audit

Preserve direct todo/in_progress/done transitions. A Done task at Completed Sprint location reopened to either todo or in_progress has effective todo/Backlog, null location_sprint_id and an appended exact backlog_position under Project lock. Existing 003 trigger advances backlog_revision once; do not double-increment it. Preserve Completed Sprint and completed allocations; no mutable Task timestamp is added. Actual completeSprint/allocateTask races remain an SP-05 integration gate.

Allocate blocker sequence under the common Project/Task boundary with explicit revision/sequence bounds. Highest committed per-task sequence determines blocked, not time or ID. History pages require current Task/project read authority without audit-read. Proposed bounded HMAC cursors bind actor/project/task/route/order/page size/membership generation/complete event projection/expiry; reuse page size50 and TTL300 seconds. A new login alone does not invalidate the actor's cursor. Malformed/foreign400 and verified stale/expired409 return no items; clear accumulated pages and restart. No cache or permission fallback is introduced.

Audit retains actor/time/action/entity and resolvable before/after content/state/assignment/placement or blocker-event identity. Use bounded unambiguous structured references and retained immutable source identities when reconstruction is claimed; neither a concatenated raw title nor an unresolvable digest suffices. Audit-read never substitutes for Task/history read, and operational reads confer no private authority-audit access.

### Additive migration and verification gates

Applied 001–009 remain immutable. A separately briefed future additive migration refuses ambiguous new-operation identities, unprovenanced selected grants/audits and unsupported legacy semantics; no guessed backfill. Down refuses retained new grants (including invalidated ones), outcomes/events or dependent authority/business audit; empty-compatible reverse restores exact 009 functions/constraints. Keep historical 006/008/009 fixture ceilings and use explicit new-schema disposable fixtures for forward/reverse/repeat, malformed/null/unsafe validation, runtime issue/revival denial and data-refusal tests. No migration is authored or applied by P03A2.

Future producer evidence must cover old-operation regressions, new grants/removal/rejoin, disabled/null assignment, both removal/assignment orderings, post-wait expiry, replay after later state/eligibility/revision changes, revoked replay denial, no-op recovery, sequence/overflow, audit/outcome rollback and unknown acknowledgement. Permission and transport behaviour need actual handlers; SQL/schema/source checks are prerequisites only. P05 UI refresh/conflict/unknown recovery and P08 actual Sprint producer races remain required, not deferred Must scope.

## Transport reconciliation and alternatives

Keep current Error/Task/Blocker wire schemas and operation count. C01: generic409 state_conflict has no current_revision; client reads getTask under current authority. C02: Blocker201 acknowledges only the event; fresh Task/history supplies current blocked/revision. C03: known rollback differs from unknown acknowledgement; existing503/transport failure is not a new pending wire object. Existing413/415 declarations from P03A are not Fastify evidence.

Rejected policy alternatives were implicit edit via create, membership-only disabled-target eligibility and automatic original-result expiry/current-row substitution. Extra conflict/event fields would require a wire change and are unnecessary for the selected refresh flow. A coarse task-mutate grant would collapse independent requested actions. None is adopted here.

## Consequences and current evidence

Separating grants requires private provisioning and DB checks before usable mutation handlers. Permanent receipts intentionally retain owner-entered Task text; current-authority replay protects disclosure but is not automatic erasure. Exact retained before/after sources and serialized writes cost storage and may constrain throughput; capacity is unmeasured. No load balancing, charts, scheduler or new service is selected.

P03A2 aligns source and planned verification only. Its [result](../implementation/features/sp-04-update-task/reviews/p03a2-source-alignment.md) records actual structural checks and preservation limits. The owning plan must refine/register P03B before storage/test implementation; no code, runtime permission or formal ADR acceptance is claimed here.

# Update work state and record blockers

**Artifact ID:** SP-04  
**Version/date:** 0.7.3 Draft · 3 November 2026
**Status:** Draft for owner review; ADR-0007–ADR-0017 directions are owner-confirmed; application acceptance remains unproven.\
**Inputs:** PRD-01 v0.10.1; [architecture](../docs/architecture.md); [use case](../docs/sdlc/use-cases.md#uc-04--update-work-state-and-record-blockers); [contract pack](../contracts/README.md) v0.25.1; PLAN-01 v0.4.\; Proposed ADR-0028 v0.1
**Author:** development agent acting sequentially; owner reviews business choices.

**Status:** Unimplemented. **Target:** Month 1.  
**Dependencies:** SP-03.   
**Trace:** FR-09, FR-40, FR-43, FR-44; BR-03, BR-02, BR-06; SC-03, SC-04.

## Goal and contract

Update a task without stale overwrite and retain blocker resolution evidence.

Use workspace service contract in contracts/openapi/. Operation IDs: editTask, setTaskState, setAssignee, recordBlocker. Server identity/permission is never asserted in client fields. SP-11 captures records inside every producing operation.

## Input/output and edges

Input: valid session, operation-specific fields, expected revision and scoped idempotency key where required. Output: confirmed owned record/evidence with server identity/revision, or explicit validation/conflict/denial/pending/provider failure. Test invalid/unknown input, denied target, stale request, duplicate key, membership removal/rejoin, source replacement/deletion and service outage where relevant. No protected content in error/log output.

## Acceptance

1. For new operations, expected revision mismatch returns generic409 state_conflict and preserves the newer update; client reads getTask under current authority, without an extra current_revision field. Committed original-key replay follows acceptance7.
2. A new non-null assignee must be an enabled current member of the same project; unknown, nonmember, foreign-project and disabled targets are rejected after caller Task/action checks without changing the prior assignee. Null unassign is allowed with current assignment authority.
3. Latest committed sequence Open means blocked; latest Resolved means unblocked, with ordered append-only history. Blocker201 acknowledges the event only; UI refreshes current Task/history for blocked/revision. Every distinct accepted event advances Task revision; same-key replay does not append again.
4. Any direct change between To Do, In Progress and Done is allowed for an authorised member with the expected revision, including reopening Done. Persist audit and expose the committed result on refresh; no automatic Scrum Master approval.
5. Reopen a Done task from a Completed Sprint: atomically set To Do and return it to Product Backlog (including a requested In Progress reopen target), preserve completed allocation history and keep the Sprint Completed. Race reopening against Sprint completion/allocation; no stale overwrite or two current allocations is allowed (ADR-0008 v0.3).

6. New Backlog content edits require separate edit authority; creator, create-only backlog-author and role labels grant none. Every new write and original-result replay requires current session, Task/project read scope and the exact requested action.
7. Retain original edit/state/assignment200 Task (including title/description) and blocker201 indefinitely with consumed actor/operation/key/hash. Committed same-input replay returns the historical original after current authority checks, without applying live write revision/old assignee eligibility/placement or mutating again; current UI state comes from fresh reads. Changed input conflicts. Known pre-commit failure rolls back business/audit/outcome together; lost acknowledgement remains unknown and reconciles only the original identity/body.

## Allowed paths and Done

Runtime implementation paths: services/workspace/**, apps/web/**, tests/workspace/**. Shared sources are read dependencies except for the explicitly registered coordinated support slices below. No other-service database writes.

**Coordinated SP-04 source support:** [FEAT-SP04-01](../docs/implementation/features/sp-04-update-task/plan.md) owns current small-task status. P03A transport declarations/metadata were reconciled by its coordinator; historical preregistration evidence limits remain in that disposition. P03A2 is explicitly owner-requested and registered before further source edits: docs/sdlc/PRD_SRS.md (existing AC rows), docs/sdlc/use-cases.md (UC-03 edit and UC-04), docs/sdlc/data-design.md, docs/sdlc/api-design.md, contracts/README.md, contracts/data-model.json (existing metadata/constraints only), this spec, docs/sdlc/test-plan.md, test-coverage.md, requirement-verification.md, new Proposed docs/adr/0028-task-mutation-authority-and-outcomes.md and docs/adr/README.md. The owning feature folder/registers, ADR index, manifest/generated metadata and required current input/version aliases with patch registrations are support scope as enumerated in [SP04-P03A2](../docs/implementation/features/sp-04-update-task/tasks/P03A2-policy-source-alignment.md). No existing ADR, BRD/baseline, OpenAPI schema, runtime, migration or test implementation changes belong to P03A2. Future P03B code/storage changes need their own exact brief and additive migration tests.

Current commands: npm run context:check and npm run context:test validate context/contracts only.

Done requires the matching PRD ACs exercised on real handlers/persisted state; relevant unit and consumer/provider contract checks; access/version/concurrency/failure negatives; visible UI result where appropriate; evidence in backlog and no known unauthorised access. Add real application build/test/lint commands only when those entry points exist. This draft is reviewable, not a finished runnable application task.

## Assumptions/checklist/handoff

Uses the applicable owner-confirmed directions through ADR-0017 and OWNER-Q-01. Additional delegation, physical retention, OD-09 identity and OD-12 framework details stay open. Pass for goal/trace/input-output/edges/paths/Done; Gap for accepted policy/contract/stack and runtime tests. Handoff: proceed under confirmed directions; resolve only remaining decisions relevant to implementation. No settled policy requires repeat approval.

ADR-0017: assignment checks current membership and serializes against removal. Member removal clears current assignee and increments task revision without changing state/allocation/history; rejoin never reassigns automatically.

**17 October input reconciliation:** FR-09/40/43/44, ADR-0008 and OWNER-Q-01: direct transitions and Completed-Sprint reopening to Backlog/To Do are retained. Reviewed against the current requirement rows and operation ownership. This is specification review, not implementation or full AC coverage evidence.

## Operational reconstruction correction — 18 October 2026

Use listBlockerEvents for member-facing history in ascending sequence. Test current membership on every page, empty history, foreign/stale cursor rejection and reconstruction after reconnect. No audit-read dependency. See [ADR-0018](../docs/adr/0018-operational-read-projections.md). No application acceptance is claimed.

## Reopen persistence follow-up — 18 October 2026

Proposed ADR-0018/migration 003 persist current placement separately. Test complete in A, reopen Backlog/To Do, mark Done in Backlog, then allocate to B while A's completed association remains unchanged. Placement changes bump task revision; crossing the Backlog boundary changes backlog_revision. Rejected/rolled-back writes preserve both. Current read authority/audit/handler evidence remains required.

## Input metadata reconciliation — 25 October 2026

Only input-version metadata is synchronized for the bounded architecture/UC/checklist corrections. Requirements, acceptance assertions, design body and prior observations are unchanged; no complete semantic review or runtime check is implied.

## Transport contract support reconciliation — 3 November 2026

Workspace contract v0.2.13 declares bounded HTTP 413 and 415 error responses for editTask, setTaskState, setAssignee and recordBlocker. Handlers and database migrations remain unimplemented at this support checkpoint.

[SP04-OWNER-01](../docs/implementation/features/sp-04-update-task/owner-decisions.md) records actual decisions; [ADR-0028](../docs/adr/0028-task-mutation-authority-and-outcomes.md) remains Proposed mechanics. AC-09/40/43/44 and UC-03/04 are aligned without new IDs/priorities or wire schema changes. The [owning plan](../docs/implementation/features/sp-04-update-task/plan.md) controls current preparation and future producer briefs. Structural checks do not satisfy real-handler/persisted-state Done or actual SP-05 integration.
